romaji: Ōkuninushi kara kuni o moratta ten no kamisama wa dō shimashita ka?
english: What did the heavenly deity do after being handed over the country by Ōkuninushi?
exampleRomaji: Ōkuninushi kara kuni o yuzurareta ten no kamisama wa dō shimashita ka?
japaneseFurigana: 大国主(おおくにぬし)から国(くに)をもらった天(てん)の神様(かみさま)はどうしましたか？
exampleEn: What did the heavenly deity do after being handed over the country by Ōkuninushi?
audioPath: clips/001_大国主から国をもらった甘の神様はどうしましたか.wav
grammar2:
大国主(おおくにぬし) = Ōkuninushi (name of deity)
譲(ゆず)る = to hand over ↔ もらう = to receive

romaji: Amaterasu no mago no Niniginomikoto ga ten kara chijō ni oriru koto ni narimashita.
english: It was decided that Niniginomikoto, the grandson of Amaterasu, would descend from heaven to earth.
exampleRomaji: Amaterasu no mago no Niniginomikoto ga ten kara chijō ni oriru koto ni narimashita.
japaneseFurigana: アマテラスの孫(まご)のニニギノミコトが天(てん)から地上(ちじょう)に降(お)りることになりました。
exampleEn: It was decided that Niniginomikoto, the grandson of Amaterasu, would descend from heaven to earth.
audioPath: clips/002_アマテラスの孫のニニギの御子とが天から地上に降りることになりました。.wav
grammar2: 降(お)りる = to descend ↔ 上(のぼ)る = to ascend

romaji: Amaterasu no mago ga chijō ni iku no desu ne?
english: So, Amaterasu's grandson is going to earth, right?
exampleRomaji: Amaterasu no mago ga chijō ni iku no desu ne?
japaneseFurigana: アマテラスの孫(まご)が地上(ちじょう)に行(い)くのですね？
exampleEn: So, Amaterasu's grandson is going to earth, right?
audioPath: clips/003_アマテラスの孫が地上に行くのですね.wav

romaji: Hai.
english: Yes.
exampleRomaji: Hai.
japaneseFurigana: はい。
exampleEn: Yes.
audioPath: clips/004_はい。.wav

romaji: Amaterasu wa Niniginomikoto ni okome no inaho to sanshu no takaramono o watashimashita.
english: Amaterasu gave Niniginomikoto rice ears and three sacred treasures.
exampleRomaji: Amaterasu wa Niniginomikoto ni okome no inaho to sanshu no takaramono o watashimashita.
japaneseFurigana: アマテラスはニニギノミコトにお米(こめ)の稲穂(いなほ)と三(さん)つの宝物(たからもの)を渡(わた)しました。
exampleEn: Amaterasu gave Niniginomikoto rice ears and three sacred treasures.
audioPath: clips/005_アマテラスはニニギの御子にお米の稲穂と三つの宝物を渡しました。.wav

romaji: Sanshu no takaramono ni tsuite wa ato de kuwashiku kikitai desu.
english: I would like to hear more details about the three sacred treasures later.
exampleRomaji: Sanshu no takaramono ni tsuite wa ato de kuwashiku kikitai desu.
japaneseFurigana: 三(さん)つの宝物(たからもの)については後(あと)で詳(くわ)しく聞(き)きたいです。
exampleEn: I would like to hear more details about the three sacred treasures later.
audioPath: clips/006_三つの宝物については後で詳しく聞きたいです。.wav

romaji: Niniginomikoto wa Nihon no doko ni orimashita ka?
english: Where in Japan did Niniginomikoto descend to?
exampleRomaji: Niniginomikoto wa Nihon no doko ni orimashita ka?
japaneseFurigana: ニニギノミコトは日本(にほん)のどこに降(お)りましたか？
exampleEn: Where in Japan did Niniginomikoto descend to?
audioPath: clips/007_ニニギの御子とは日本のどこに降りましたか.wav

romaji: Kyūshū no Takachiho to iu yama no teppen desu.
english: It is the peak of a mountain called Takachiho in Kyushu.
exampleRomaji: Kyūshū no Takachiho to iu yama no teppen desu.
japaneseFurigana: 九州(きゅうしゅう)の高千穂(たかちほ)という山(やま)のてっぺんです。
exampleEn: It is the peak of a mountain called Takachiho in Kyushu.
audioPath: clips/008_九州の高千歩という山のてっぺんです。.wav
grammar2: てっぺん = peak/top ≒ 山頂(さんちょう) = summit

romaji: Takachiho desu ne.
english: Takachiho, right?
exampleRomaji: Takachiho desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 高千穂(たかちほ)ですね。
exampleEn: Takachiho, right?
audioPath: clips/009_高千歩ですね。.wav

romaji: Ten kara oriru koto o nan to iimasu ka?
english: What is the term for descending from heaven?
exampleRomaji: Ten kara oriru koto o nan to iimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 天(てん)から降(お)りることを何(なん)と言(い)いますか？
exampleEn: What is the term for descending from heaven?
audioPath: clips/010_天から降りることを何と言いますか.wav

romaji: Tenson kōrin to iimasu.
english: It is called the 'Descent of the Heavenly Grandchild.'
exampleRomaji: Tenson kōrin to iimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 天孫(てんそん)降臨(こうりん)といいます。
exampleEn: It is called the 'Descent of the Heavenly Grandchild.'
audioPath: clips/011_天村降臨と言います。.wav
grammar2:
天孫(てんそん) = Heavenly Grandchild
降臨(こうりん) = descent of a deity

romaji: Amaterasu no mago ga orite kuru to iu imi desu.
english: It means that the grandson of Amaterasu descends to earth.
exampleRomaji: Amaterasu no mago ga orite kuru to iu imi desu.
japaneseFurigana: アマテラスの孫(まご)が降(お)りてくるという意味(いみ)です。
exampleEn: It means that the grandson of Amaterasu descends to earth.
audioPath: clips/012_アマテラスの孫が降りてくるという意味です。.wav

romaji: Oriru toki michi wa wakarimashita ka?
english: Did you know the way when you descended?
exampleRomaji: Oriru toki michi wa wakarimashita ka?
japaneseFurigana: 降(お)りるとき道(みち)はわかりましたか？
exampleEn: Did you know the way when you descended?
audioPath: clips/013_降りるとき道はわかりましたか.wav

romaji: Tochū no michi ni totemo karada ga ōkikute me ga hikatte iru ayashii kamisama ga tatte imashita.
english: On the way, there was a suspicious deity with a huge body and glowing eyes standing there.
exampleRomaji: Tochū no michi ni totemo karada ga ōkikute me ga hikatte iru ayashii kamisama ga tatte imashita.
japaneseFurigana: 途(と)中(ちゅう)の道(みち)にとても体(からだ)が大(おお)きくて目(め)が光(ひか)っている怪(あや)しい神(かみ)様(さま)が立(た)っていました。
exampleEn: On the way, there was a suspicious deity with a huge body and glowing eyes standing there.
audioPath: clips/014_途中の道にとても体が大きくて目が光っている怪しい神様が立っていました。.wav

romaji: Teki desu ka?
english: Is it an enemy?
exampleRomaji: Teki desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 敵(てき)ですか？
exampleEn: Is it an enemy?
audioPath: clips/015_敵ですか.wav

romaji: Kowai desu ne.
english: That's scary, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Kowai desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 怖(こわ)いですね。
exampleEn: That's scary, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/016_怖いですね。.wav

exampleRomaji: Iie, Sarutahiko to iu chijō no kamisama desu.
japaneseFurigana: いいえ、サルタヒコという地上(ちじょう)の神(かみ)様(さま)です。
exampleEn: No, it is Sarutahiko, a deity of the earth.
audioPath: clips/017_いいえ、サルタヒコという地上の神様です。.wav

romaji: Niniginomikoto no michi-annai o suru tame ni matte imashita.
english: He was waiting to guide Niniginomikoto on his way.
exampleRomaji: Ninigi no Michi annai o suru tame ni matte imashita.
japaneseFurigana: ニニギノミコトの道(みち)案(あん)内(ない)をするために待(ま)っていました。
exampleEn: He was waiting to guide Ninigi-no-Mikoto on his way.
audioPath: clips/018_ニニギの御子との道案内をするために待っていました。.wav
grammar2: 道(みち)案(あん)内(ない) = guide/guidance

romaji: Annai-nin ga ita no desu ne.
english: So there was a guide after all.
exampleRomaji: Annai-nin ga ita no desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 案(あん)内(ない)人(にん)がいたのですね。
exampleEn: So there was a guide after all.
audioPath: clips/019_案内人がいたのですね。.wav

romaji: Yokatta desu.
english: That's a relief.
exampleRomaji: Yokatta desu.
japaneseFurigana: よかったです。
exampleEn: That's a relief.
audioPath: clips/020_よかったです。.wav

romaji: Sarutahiko no annai de Niniginomikoto wa buji ni Takachiho ni tsukimashita.
english: With Sarutahiko's guidance, Niniginomikoto safely arrived at Takachiho.
exampleRomaji: Sarutahiko no annai de Niniginomikoto wa buji ni Takachihoni tsukimashita.
japaneseFurigana: サルタヒコの案内(あんない)でニニギノミコトは無事(ぶじ)に高千穂(たかちほ)に着(つ)きました。
exampleEn: With Sarutahiko's guidance, Niniginomikoto safely arrived at Takachiho.
audioPath: clips/021_サルタヒコの案内でニニギの御子とは無事に高千歩に着きました。.wav
grammar2: 無事(ぶじ)に = safely ↔ 危(あぶ)なく = dangerously

romaji: Tsuita ato nani o shimashita ka?
english: What did he do after arriving?
exampleRomaji: Tsuita ato nani o shimashita ka?
japaneseFurigana: 着(つ)いた後(あと)何をしましたか？
exampleEn: What did he do after arriving?
audioPath: clips/022_着いた後何をしましたか.wav

romaji: Soko ni rippa na kyūden o tatete, Amaterasu kara moratta okome o Nihonjū ni hiromemashita.
english: He built a magnificent palace there and spread the rice he received from Amaterasu throughout Japan.
exampleRomaji: Soko ni rippa na kyūden o tatete, Amaterasu kara moratta okome o Nihon-jū ni hiromemashita.
japaneseFurigana: そこに立(りっ)派(ぱ)な宮殿(きゅうでん)を建(た)てて、アマテラスからもらったお米(こめ)を日本中(にほんじゅう)に広(ひろ)めました。
exampleEn: He built a magnificent palace there and spread the rice he received from Amaterasu throughout Japan.
audioPath: clips/023_そこに立派な宮殿を建ててアマテラスからもらったお米を日本中に広めました。.wav
grammar2:
立(りっ)派(ぱ) = magnificent
広(ひろ)める = to spread

romaji: Dakara Nihonjin wa okome o takusan taberu no desu ne.
english: So that's why Japanese people eat a lot of rice, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Dakara Nihonjin wa okome o takusan taberu no desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: だから日本(にほん)人(じん)はお米(こめ)をたくさん食(た)べるのですね。
exampleEn: So that's why Japanese people eat a lot of rice, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/024_だから日本人はお米をたくさん食べるのですね。.wav

romaji: Sō desu.
english: That's right.
exampleRomaji: Sō desu.
japaneseFurigana: そうです。
exampleEn: That's right.
audioPath: clips/025_そうです。.wav

romaji: Nihon no nōgyō to okome no bunka wa kono kamisama kara hajimarimashita.
english: Japan's agriculture and rice culture began with this deity.
exampleRomaji: Nihon no nōgyō to okome no bunka wa kono kamisama kara hajimarimashita.
japaneseFurigana: 日本(にほん)の農(のう)業(ぎょう)とお米(こめ)の文化(ぶんか)はこの神(かみ)様(さま)から始(はじ)まりました。
exampleEn: Japan's agriculture and rice culture began with this deity.
audioPath: clips/026_日本の農業とお米の文化はこの神様から始まりました。.wav

romaji: Niniginomikoto wa chijō de kekkon shimashita ka?
english: Did Niniginomikoto get married on earth?
exampleRomaji: Niniginomikoto wa chijō de kekkon shimashita ka?
japaneseFurigana: ニニギノミコトは地(ち)上(じょう)で結婚(けっこん)しましたか？
exampleEn: Did Niniginomikoto get married on earth?
audioPath: clips/027_ニニギの御子とは地上で結婚しましたか.wav

romaji: Hai.
english: Yes, he did.
exampleRomaji: Hai.
japaneseFurigana: はい。
exampleEn: Yes, he did.
audioPath: clips/028_はい。.wav

exampleRomaji: Konohanasakuyahime to iu sakura no yō ni utsukushii yama no kamisama no musume to kekkon shimashita.
japaneseFurigana: コノハナサクヤヒメという桜(さくら)のように美(うつく)しい山(やま)の神(かみ)様(さま)の娘(むすめ)と結婚(けっこん)しました。
exampleEn: He married Konohanasakuyahime, the daughter of a mountain deity who was as beautiful as a cherry blossom.
audioPath: clips/029_この花咲くや姫という桜のように美しい山の神様の娘と結婚しました。.wav

romaji: Kirei na namae desu ne.
english: That's a beautiful name, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Kirei na namae desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 綺(き)麗(れい)な名前(なまえ)ですね。
exampleEn: That's a beautiful name, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/030_綺麗な名前ですね。.wav

romaji: Kono Niniginomikoto no shison ga nochi ni Nihon no saisho no tennō ni narimasu.
english: The descendants of Niniginomikoto later became the first emperor of Japan.
exampleRomaji: Kono Ninigi-no-Mikoto no shison ga nochi ni Nihon no saisho no tennō ni narimasu.
japaneseFurigana: このニニギノミコトの子孫(しそん)が後(のち)に日本(にほん)の最初(さいしょ)の天皇(てんのう)になります。
exampleEn: The descendants of Ninigi-no-Mikoto later became the first emperor of Japan.
audioPath: clips/031_このニニギの御子との子孫が後に日本の最初の天皇になります。.wav
grammar2: 子孫(しそん) = descendant ↔ 先祖(せんぞ) = ancestor

romaji: Kamisama kara tennō ni tsunagatte iku no desu ne.
english: So, the lineage connects from the gods to the emperor, doesn't it?
exampleRomaji: Kamisama kara tennō ni tsunagatte iku no desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 神様(かみさま)から天皇(てんのう)に繋(つな)がっていくのですね。
exampleEn: So, the lineage connects from the gods to the emperor, doesn't it?
audioPath: clips/032_神様から天皇に繋がっていくのですね。.wav

romaji: Hai.
english: Yes.
exampleRomaji: Hai.
japaneseFurigana: はい。
exampleEn: Yes.
audioPath: clips/033_はい。.wav

romaji: Nihon no tennōke ga totemo nagai rekishi o motte iru riyū wa kono shinwa ga aru kara desu.
english: The reason why Japan's imperial family has such a long history is because of this myth.
exampleRomaji: Nihon no tennōke ga totemo nagai rekishi o motte iru riyū wa kono shinwa ga aru kara desu.
japaneseFurigana: 日本(にほん)の天皇家(てんのうけ)がとても長(なが)い歴史(れきし)を持(も)っている理由(りゆう)はこの神話(しんわ)があるからです。
exampleEn: The reason why Japan's imperial family has such a long history is because of this myth.
audioPath: clips/034_日本の天皇家がとても長い歴史を持っている理由はこの神話があるからです。.wav

romaji: Shinwa to ima no Nihon ga tsunagatte ite omoshiroi desu.
english: It's fascinating how the myth connects to present-day Japan.
exampleRomaji: Shinwa to ima no Nihon ga tsunagatte ite omoshiroi desu.
japaneseFurigana: 神話(しんわ)と今(いま)の日本(にほん)が繋(つな)がっていて面白(おもしろ)いです。
exampleEn: It's fascinating how the myth connects to present-day Japan.
audioPath: clips/035_神話と今の日本が繋がっていて面白いです。.wav

romaji: Miyazaki-ken ni wa ima demo kono Tenson Kōrin no butai ga takusan nokotte imasu yo.
english: In Miyazaki Prefecture, many sites related to the descent of the heavenly grandson still remain even today.
exampleRomaji: Miyazaki-ken ni wa ima demo kono Tenson Kōrin no butai ga takusan nokotte imasu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 宮崎県(みやざきけん)には今(いま)でもこの天孫降臨(てんそんこうりん)の舞台(ぶたい)がたくさん残(のこ)っていますよ。
exampleEn: In Miyazaki Prefecture, many sites related to the descent of the heavenly grandson still remain even today.
audioPath: clips/036_宮崎県には今でもこの天孫降臨の舞台がたくさん残っていますよ。.wav
